summary: Key issues included the validity of the appellant's claims under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, including Stridhana recovery, domestic violence, and property rights after her husband's death. The Trial Court found in favor of the appellant, awarding compensation, return of Stridhana (excluding car), and property rights. The High Court upheld the reversal of this decision by the First Appellate Court, which held that the appellant never resided with the respondents in the shared household, undermining her claims under the D.V. Act. The Supreme Court examined factual inconsistencies, particularly regarding residence, Stridhana possession, and paternity denial as emotional abuse. The issue centered on whether the appellant suffered domestic violence and was entitled to reliefs under Sections 12, 19, and 22 of the D.V. Act.
legal_provisions_cited: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Section 1(d)(iii)
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Section 12
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Section 19
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Section 22
final_judgment: The appeal was disposed of, with the Supreme Court affirming that the appellant had established her case of domestic violence and entitlement to reliefs under the D.V. Act, thereby setting aside the High Court judgment and restoring the Trial Court's order for return of Stridhana, compensation of Rs.10,000, and protection of property rights.
